cases.title: Three Patients, One Ambulance
cases.presentation: Night call to a rural two-car head-on collision 40 minutes from the nearest hospital. You are the only unit; the next is 30 minutes away. You find three critically injured patients.
cases.question: Is this an MCI?
options: A: No — MCIs need at least 10 patients.
B: Only if a hospital declares it.
C: Yes — casualties exceed immediately available resources; declare and request resources.
D: Only if one patient dies.
cases.explanation: MCI = patients > resources. Three critical patients for one crew in a remote area is an MCI. Declare early so help starts moving.
cases.clinicalPearl: Small numbers + few resources = MCI. Declare early, downgrade later.

cases.title: The River Is Still Rising
cases.presentation: Flash flooding in a low-lying district. Dispatch reports 'about 12 people' stranded. As you arrive, more calls are coming in from adjacent streets; the bridge to the main hospital is closed.
cases.question: How do you classify this incident?
options: C: Open, compound — expect more victims and degraded infrastructure
cases.explanation: Victims are still appearing (open) and infrastructure is damaged (compound). Expect longer scene times, alternate destinations, and request swift-water rescue rather than entering water yourself.
cases.clinicalPearl: Open + compound = plan for self-sufficiency and longer holds.

cases.title: Week After the Storm
cases.presentation: Five days after a hurricane, your service is busier than during the storm: a chainsaw laceration, a dialysis patient with weakness and peaked T waves, an elderly woman whose home oxygen ran out, and a family with headaches.
cases.question: What is the KEY lesson?
options: A: These calls are unrelated to the disaster.
B: Disasters cause a delayed wave: CO poisoning, cleanup trauma, and decompensated chronic disease.
C: Only trauma matters after hurricanes.
D: Storm injuries are over once the wind stops.
cases.explanation: Post-disaster mortality is driven by CO from generators, cleanup injuries, and loss of dialysis, oxygen, and medications. The family with headaches needs CO screening and removal from the home.
cases.clinicalPearl: Ask every post-storm household: 'Is a generator running inside or near the house?'
